state.case_summary:
A 54-year-old man with glioblastoma treated by surgical resection began a clinical trial with M7824 (a bifunctional fusion protein targeting PD-L1 and TGF-β). Four weeks after initiation of M7824, he presented with a severely pruritic, nontender, erythematous papular and macular eruption on his back, bilateral ankles, and upper extremities. He was not receiving any other new medications. The oncology team initially classified the eruption as a grade I rash and prescribed hydrocortisone 1% cream and oral diphenhydramine, but the rash and pruritus progressed. One month later, the rash reached grade II severity, and doxycycline was started for a suspected acneiform eruption. On dermatologic evaluation, the consensus was that the eruption represented a drug reaction to M7824. Laboratory evaluation showed no elevations in liver enzymes, no eosinophilia, and no lymphadenopathy. The patient was treated with triamcinolone 0.1% ointment and hydroxyzine, but over the following two weeks the rash progressed to grade III with worsening pruritus. M7824 infusions were held, and prednisone at 40 mg per day was initiated according to guidelines, but his symptoms failed to improve.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. morbilliform drug eruption
B. acneiform eruption
C. Acneiform eruption was considered given the timing and morphology, prompting initiation of doxycycline
D. Drug
E. Immunobullous disorders were excluded by direct immunofluorescence, which showed no immune complex deposition
F. None
G. None
H. None
